single_story.note: All sources cover the Oct 6, 2026 Mistral Large 4 ('Le Chonk') preview launch.

the_news.text: On Oct 6, 2026, French AI lab Mistral released a public preview of Mistral Large 4 ('Le Chonk'), a 1-trillion-parameter model it says is the strongest open-weight model outside China, with weights due by end of October.

why_it_matters.text: Mistral pitches the model as an ownable alternative to closed US models, which the US government has restricted, and to Chinese open models; independent benchmarking so far places it below top US flagships but well ahead of the best US open-weight model.
Mistral frames cyberdefense as a key use case, arguing closed models may refuse security tasks or lose access mid-incident.

facts.text: Mistral launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4 (ML4), nicknamed 'Le Chonk', on Oct 6, 2026, available via API on Mistral Studio.
ML4 is a 1 trillion-parameter, natively multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 49 billion active parameters.
notes: NewsCord (aggregator) says 1.05 trillion total; not used as sole source.

facts.text: Weights are not yet released: Mistral says they will drop by the end of October (NewsCord, an aggregator, says Oct 27); until then it is red-teaming the model with cybersecurity leaders, vetted partners and state authorities, who get a version with reduced moderation and expanded cyber capabilities.
notes: TechCrunch says 'in just three weeks' and that it is 'not an open-weight model yet', accessible via a public guardrail endpoint.

facts.text: [CLAIM: Mistral says] ML4 is state-of-the-art among open models on cybersecurity, finance and law, competitive with the strongest open-source models globally, and significantly outperforms any open-weight model from the US or Europe.
notes: WIRED: Mistral presents it as by far the most capable open-weight model developed outside China and 'very, very close' to some proprietary models.

facts.text: Independent benchmarker Artificial Analysis' early testing places ML4 preview on its intelligence leaderboard between DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and OpenAI's entry-level GPT6 Luna, at a major disadvantage to OpenAI and Anthropic flagships, but well ahead of the top US open-weights model, Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling.
notes: Single-source (Register's description of Artificial Analysis results). The Register says Mistral's own benchmarks tell a 'far rosier' story and advises a grain of salt. TechCrunch notes benchmark results are still pending.

facts.text: [CLAIM: Mistral says] ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in its own European datacenters, on data spanning more than 160 languages.
notes: TechCrunch (quoting Pierre Stock) and WIRED-aggregator NewsCord say about 4,000 GPUs; Stock says this is two to three times fewer than Chinese competitors. NewsCord says two months of training.

facts.text: WIRED reports Chinese labs have been accused by the US government of abusing distillation, whereas Mistral claims it trained its model from scratch.

[CLAIM: Mistral says] On the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index ML4 ranks in the top five models globally and leads non-Chinese open-weight models by a wide margin; it scores 82% on a vulnerability reproduce-and-patch test and 93% on Cybench.
notes: Mistral says Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra score near zero on the test because they refuse. The Register repeats that Mistral claims strong cyber performance.

facts.text: Mistral says it ranks second of five in a blind human coding evaluation by Surge AI (3.74), behind only Claude Opus 5 (4.22).
notes: Mistral-reported; the evaluation was commissioned by Mistral per the blog's wording ('we ran').

facts.text: Mistral argues provider-level refusals can block legitimate vulnerability research, and losing access to a capability mid-incident can itself be a security risk.
Mistral says ML4 is optimized for coding, cyberdefense and niche domains like manufacturing, finance and electrical engineering; TechCrunch adds chip design, relevant to backers ASML and Samsung.

WIRED reports that in June the Trump administration placed temporary restrictions on distribution of OpenAI and Anthropic models over cyberattack concerns, creating an opening for Mistral's open-weight models.

Mistral says ML4 is the first milestone funded by its €3 billion Series D, which it calls the largest equity round ever raised by a European technology company; it expects large improvements in coming weeks and months as RL training continues.
notes: WIRED gives the September round as $3.3 billion at a $24 billion valuation, the largest ever raise by a European tech company; TechCrunch says Samsung led the Series D at €21 billion valuation (about $24.39 billion).

background.text: Mistral has generally lagged US rivals on model performance, revenue and release frequency, but in September raised a $3.3 billion round at a $24 billion valuation and its earnings have reportedly increased 20-fold in about a year.
Growing US-Europe tension and the US restrictions on frontier model distribution have strengthened the case for European 'AI sovereignty'.
notes: TechCrunch cites Macron's 'third way in AI'.

quotes.text: Mistral is still in the race of getting the best model. This is the main message.
quotes.speaker: Guillaume Lample
notes: Original WIRED text: “Mistral is still in the race of getting the best model,” Lample says. “This is the main message.”

quotes.text: Sometimes, people like to [make a big deal] over the US, versus Europe, versus China. But what really matters is to own the model—even for US companies. If you use a closed model, there is no guarantee it will still be there tomorrow.
quotes.speaker: Guillaume Lample

quotes.text: In the meantime, we’ll work with trusted partners and governments to make sure that the open source weights can be used to defend, but not to [perform] malicious attacks,
quotes.speaker: Pierre Stock

quotes.text: which is two to three times less than our Chinese competitors, and significantly less than the closed source competitors,
quotes.speaker: Pierre Stock
quotes.where: Told TechCrunch, about 4,000 Nvidia GPUs used

quotes.text: The continental strategy of the EU to become more technologically sovereign … and the increased hostility of the US is a magic formula that all of a sudden puts Mistral—whose performance has not been spectacular—in a favorable position,
quotes.speaker: Andrea Renda

terms.name: Open-weight model
terms.definition: A model whose trained weights are released so anyone can run and customize it; WIRED notes businesses then pay only for the compute they use.

terms.name: Distillation
terms.definition: Training a smaller model on the outputs of a larger one.

terms.name: Mixture of experts (MoE)
terms.definition: An architecture that activates only part of the model's parameters (about 49 billion of 1 trillion here) per query to keep serving costs low.

not_answered: Final benchmark results: TechCrunch says benchmark results are still pending; only Mistral's own and early Artificial Analysis results exist.
Hardware requirements to run the model: Mistral gave no guidance (The Register).
Exact weights release date and licence terms: 'end of the month' per Mistral; Oct 27 only via an aggregator.
Independent confirmation of Mistral's cybersecurity claims and 'best open-weight outside China' claim beyond the Register's Artificial Analysis note.
